searchText: <@!689161464829050960> painted his parking lot 😐 Also, still working on https://github.com/SamWilsn/docutils-rst-writer is there a canonical genesis json spec somewhere? or is it a looser client-by-client thing where there happens to be some overlap in genesis json format? I believe there isn't <@!524738020033691659> - I know Parity had a very different format to other clients "by design" Not sure what the rationale/difference was, though I am looking at the baseFeePerGas in genesis json config. I presume that means the baseFeePerGas for the genesis block, but I am wondering if it is just the first baseFee for the first fee market block generally. Where can I find the history on this field? Good question 😶 <@!524738020033691659> there is no genesis spec unfortunately, it's client specific. > I am looking at the baseFeePerGas in genesis json config. I presume that means the baseFeePerGas for the genesis block, but I am wondering if it is just the first baseFee for the first fee market block generally. Where can I find the history on this field? I would expect that it is defining the `baseFeePerGas` for the genesis block this is pretty telling: https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/blob/master/core/genesis.go#L60-L65 "do not use!" <@!543900561460822016> do you know offhand if geth provides cli args to modify the default basefee for the first london block? doing some besu code cleanup and it has experimental parameters to override initialBaseFee, slack coefficient, and max change denominator. I am debating whether we should even continue to offer them or leave them at the eip1559 spec. I am leaning towards just removing them, and any new networks that have london enabled will defer to the 1559 mainnet spec values as far as i know, there isn't a cli arg like that in geth <@!524738020033691659> one note about Besu isn’t that 1559 isn’t _great_ in networks where the blocks are mostly empty. It’s not the end of the world to have it, but it’s worth considering that for private network or other networks where raising the gas limit is easy (like Palm, for instance), 1559 may add complexity and little to no value Oh wait I perhaps misunderstood: if you are saying that given a network which *wants* 1559, does it make sense to make the stating base fee / slack coefficient customizable? In that case I’d say no

"do not use!"

excerpts.author: suburbandad_
excerpts.content:
doing some besu code cleanup and it has experimental parameters to override initialBaseFee, slack coefficient, and max change denominator.  

I am debating whether we should even continue to offer them or leave them at the eip1559 spec.  I am leaning towards just removing them, and any new networks that have london enabled will defer to the 1559 mainnet spec values

excerpts.author: lightclient
excerpts.content: as far as i know, there isn't a cli arg like that in geth
